01.event: Rav Ami permits first intercourse on Shabbat; the Sages object that the ketubah is not written
01.turn: He answers: have her seize movable property as a pledge
01.outcome: No narrated outcome beyond his answer
01.summary: Rav Ami permitted a man to consummate his marriage on Shabbat. The Sages objected that her marriage contract had not been written. He told them to have her seize movables as security.
01.missing: Any event beyond the ruling and the exchange; no one is said to act on it
01.reason: Mostly speech acts around a ruling, but there is a challenge and an implied change in practice; by R-C2 that is borderline rather than a story.

02.missing: Any narrated event; it is a first-person statement about his marriage age
02.reason: A dictum attributing his superiority to marrying at sixteen; a bare self-report with nothing following.

03.actor: A half-slave half-free woman and her master
03.event: The court forced her master to emancipate her
03.outcome: She became a free woman; the Gemara then discusses whose opinion this follows
03.summary: An incident is reported of a woman who was half slave and half free. They compelled her master, and he made her free. The Gemara then asks which tanna's view this follows.
03.missing: Why they compelled him, the woman's situation and any aftermath are not narrated in the passage
03.reason: There is a real incident with a coercive act and a change of status, but it is told in one line and serves a legal discussion; between story and not, borderline.

04.missing: Any event beyond a permission and its reason
04.reason: A report of a ruling about a mortar in Mar Shmuel's house, cited for the halakha; nothing happens and no one responds.

05.event: Funeral costs were so heavy that relatives abandoned their dead and fled
05.turn: Rabban Gamliel had himself buried in plain linen
05.outcome: Everyone followed his example; today even cheap cloth is used
05.summary: Funerals became so costly that families abandoned their dead and fled. Rabban Gamliel treated his own burial lightly and was carried out in plain linen. All the people followed him, and the practice changed.
05.reason: A situation, a sage's act in response, and a lasting change it caused: more than two actions with causality and change.

06.actor: Rav Hinnana bar Shelamiya and Rav
06.event: Rav Hinnana teaches a mishna version to Hiyya bar Rav before Rav
06.turn: Rav rebukes him for following Rabbi Meir
06.summary: Rav Hinnana taught a version of the mishna before Rav, who asked whether he had abandoned the Rabbis for Rabbi Meir. The Gemara then explains his reasoning.
06.missing: Any event beyond teaching and rebuke
06.reason: Teaching and a rebuke are ordinary scholarly discourse without conflict in R-C2's sense; the rest is the Gemara's explanation.

07.event: He habitually studied so absorbed that his cloak lay in another marketplace
07.turn: One time a man came to take the cloak
07.outcome: He found a serpent guarding it
07.summary: Rabbi Elazar ben Pedat was so absorbed in Torah that he would study in the lower market of Tzippori while his cloak lay in the upper market. Once a man came to take the cloak and found a serpent on it.
07.reason: A habitual frame followed by a one-time event with a miraculous turn; R-C3 makes that a story.

08.actor: The daughter-in-law of the house of bar Elyashiv and the orphans
08.event: She sued the orphans for her ketubah
08.turn: Embarrassed, the orphans asked her to dress properly, so she put on all her clothes
08.outcome: Before Ravina, the clothes she wore were appraised against her ketubah
08.summary: A widow was taking the orphans to court for her ketubah. They told her it shamed them for her to go in house clothes, so she dressed in all her garments. Ravina ruled that a widow's clothes on her are appraised, so their request cost them.
08.reason: An incident with several actions (suing, the orphans' request, her dressing) and an ironic consequence resolved by a ruling: R-C0's incident-plus-ruling story.

09.actor: Rabbi Hiyya bar Ami's slave and a gentile woman
09.event: The slave immersed a gentile woman for the sake of relations
09.turn: Rav Yosef says he can render her and her daughter fit
09.summary: Rabbi Hiyya bar Ami's slave immersed a gentile woman for marital purposes. Rav Yosef said he could declare her and her daughter fit to marry into Israel.
09.missing: Any second action or change beyond the one event and the ruling
09.reason: One event followed by a ruling with nothing changing afterwards; Jeff ruled this shape not a story (2026-10-25).

10.actor: A man in love with a woman (in Ilfa's addition, within the brothers' letter)
10.event: He wanted to leave Eretz Yisrael to marry her
10.turn: He heard the teaching on the merit of the Land
10.outcome: He stayed and suffered until the day he died
10.summary: Rabba's brothers wrote him a letter. In it Ilfa's addition tells of a man suffering for love of a woman who wanted to leave the Land; on hearing this teaching he stayed and suffered until his death. The rest of the letter is advice.
10.reason: Inside the letter is an embedded incident with a desire, a cause (hearing the teaching) and a lasting outcome; R-C4 counts a story embedded in speech. The advice in [3]-[4] is not part of it.

11.actor: A man and Rabbi Yitzhak Nappaha
11.event: A man says he is from Shot Mishot
11.turn: Rabbi Yitzhak Nappaha stands and declares it lies between the rivers
11.outcome: A legal discussion of lineage geography follows
11.summary: A man told the Sages he came from Shot Mishot, and Rabbi Yitzhak Nappaha stood and said it lies between the rivers. The Gemara then discusses the lineage status of that region.
11.missing: Any consequence for the man or any conflict
11.reason: A statement and a response with no conflict and no change; the rest is legal discussion.

12.event: She meant to offer her friend milk
12.turn: She mispronounced it as a curse
12.summary: A woman meaning to invite her neighbor to eat milk instead said, through bad pronunciation, may a lioness eat you.
12.reason: A single speech act cited as an example of Galilean speech, with no conflict, response or change.

13.actor: Rabbi Hanina Kara and Rabbi Yannai
13.event: Rabbi Hanina rules the halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda
13.turn: Rabbi Yannai tells him to go out and read his verses outside
13.summary: Rabbi Hanina Kara sat before Rabbi Yannai and said the halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda. Rabbi Yannai told him to go recite his verses outside, since the halakha does not.
13.missing: Any act beyond the speech; whether he was actually expelled
13.reason: Speech only, but a dismissal from the study hall is sharper conflict than ordinary debate; between not and borderline, borderline.

14.event: Rava publicly taught a ruling and Rav Pappa challenged him
14.turn: Rava appointed an amora and publicly retracted
14.summary: After Rav Pappa challenged his teaching, Rava had an amora stand before him and publicly declared his earlier statement a mistake, teaching the correct version.
14.missing: The challenge itself is in context, not the passage
14.reason: Mainly teaching (speech), but there is an act of public retraction and a change of position; borderline rather than a full story.

15.actor: The Israelites and the Midianite girls
15.event: They passed the girls before the High Priest's frontplate
15.turn: Faces of those fit for intercourse turned sallow
15.outcome: They knew which girls were which
15.summary: To know which Midianite girls were fit for intercourse, they passed them before the High Priest's frontplate; those whose faces turned sallow were known to be fit.
15.reason: An exegetical elaboration of a biblical episode (Numbers 31), which R-S1 places out of scope.

16.missing: Any event; it is a hypothetical case the Gemara constructs
16.reason: A hypothetical scenario proposed to resolve a difficulty, not an event.

17.actor: A certain man and Rav Kahana
17.event: The man let witnesses trace their names on ordinary documents
17.summary: A certain man applied the tracing leniency to ordinary documents rather than bills of divorce, and Rav Kahana had him flogged for it.
17.reason: An act followed by a punitive act that changes something, like R-C0's cow case; terse but more than a ruling.

18.event: A man bequeathed his property to Toviya and died
18.outcome: Rabbi Yohanan ruled that Toviya had come
18.summary: A man said on his deathbed his property should go to Toviya, then died. Toviya came, and Rabbi Yohanan ruled he could take it.
18.missing: Any action or change after the ruling
18.reason: A few events (the bequest, the death, the arrival) then a ruling; thin and mostly a legal case, but more than coming before a rabbi, so borderline.

19.event: A woman told Rava her husband died in a famine
19.turn: Cross-examined, she revealed she had only assumed his death
19.outcome: Rava changed his ruling: famine is like war
19.summary: Rava first held famine unlike war for a widow's testimony. A woman came and said her husband died in a famine; when Rava questioned her she answered that he surely could not have survived, showing she had not seen his death. Rava changed his view.
19.reason: The action is mainly dialogue in court, but it has a real event and a change (Rava retracts); R-C7 shape 1, borderline.

20.missing: Any narrated incident; only the manner of a collection, cited as proof
20.reason: A report of how Ravina collected the dowry, cited as evidence for the halakha, with nothing following.
